title: Westbrook Planning Board — Planning Board Meeting

fields.Location: Westbrook High School (Room 114), 125 Stroudwater St. (Hybrid via Zoom)

note: This summary highlights the meeting's key discussions and decisions, with direct quotes and timestamps for verification — it is not a substitute for watching the full meeting. Only four of nine board members were present tonight, including Vice Chair John Turcotte presiding in Chair Larry McWilliams' absence. For complete context, nuance, and anything not covered here, watch the full video at the link above. (Produced by: WestbrookCurrents.com)
attendance: Present: Vice Chair John Turcotte, Karen Axelson, Nancy Litrocapes, Kevin Price. Absent: Chair Larry McWilliams, Jason Frazier, Robin Tannenbaum, Oriana Farnham (alternate), Lucas Schrage (alternate).

blocks.x: 25-000402 — Site Plan Amendment Extension — 619 Bridgton Rd., Cloutier Properties

Ryan Russell, representing Cloutier Properties, explained that the requested one-year extension is needed. The company's engineers are still waiting for a Maine Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) response on a pending permit amendment. Supplemental information was filed with DEP in early June. Staff confirmed this is technically the first extension request under Cloutier Properties' ownership, since an earlier extension came before the project's transfer to this applicant. No public comment, no board objection. The extension is for a site plan amendment. A site plan is the detailed plan for a building project that the Planning Board reviews.
Approved by unanimous roll call, 4–0 (extending approval through May 6, 2027), moved by Kevin Price, seconded by Nancy Litrocapes.

Sean Toby (Haley Ward), Dave Andronico (JSIP Westbrook), and Aubrey Bennett (Market Square Architects) presented an updated version of a project first reviewed in a workshop in 2024. It has 228 multifamily units across seven three-story buildings on the former Twin Falls golf course (roughly 61–62 acres). Since 2024, 17 townhouses originally planned along Spring Street have been dropped. That reduces both unit count and impervious coverage. The previously DEP-reviewed stormwater design is otherwise unchanged. The plan includes 409 parking spaces (1.79 per unit), scattered covered garages, and a central clubhouse with a pool. Sewer flows to a private pump station. That station ties into the aging public Miles Lane station and upgrades it. Architecturally, the team described a “contemporary New England” style across three building types distinguished mainly by color.
No one from the public attended in person; two residents spoke remotely.
“This is a very well established large stand of a very invasive species... I would like to request that the board require an invasive species management plan for this site.”

Bonta raised concern about a roughly one-third-acre, decades-established stand of invasive Japanese knotweed near the planned ledge-removal and road area. Bonta asked that all landscaping use Maine-native species. The applicant agreed to add knotweed removal to the landscape plan and said it would look into native species. Staff noted that the City has not typically required an invasive species management plan but called it worth looking into. Paul Dryanon (Recreation & Conservation Commission) [19:43] asked whether a previously discussed trail connection to Landing Road remains part of the plan. The applicant confirmed that land south of the Stroudwater River will be formally deeded to the Presumpscot Regional Land Trust. Additional acreage could potentially be offered to support a larger trail network. A Landing Road connection depends on cooperation from other abutting landowners. Staff added that the project must provide a pedestrian connection either way. The fallback is extending the Spring Street sidewalk from Miles Lane to Landing Road.

Board members raised design and traffic questions. One member supported the native-plant request and suggested a landscaped berm along Spring Street to buffer road noise. The same member questioned the clubhouse's arched gable/cupola styling as inconsistent with the main buildings' more residential character [24:42]. Kevin Price [26:49] asked for comparative parking-ratio data from similar regional developments. Price flagged Spring Street traffic and pedestrian safety as the likely dominant concern at a future public hearing, noting the speed limit there is going from 35 to 25 mph. Price also asked about screening garage backs visible from the road. Acting Chair Turcotte proposed a board site walk, possibly in July. Turcotte also asked for an elevation rendering showing the development's appearance from Spring Street, given the road's grade change.
